Name, email address, and any information you choose to submit through forms (such as feedback, survey responses, waitlist sign-ups, or messages).

Form submissions (Google Forms):
Some data is collected through Google Forms. This may include your responses, contact details, and any additional information you voluntarily provide.

Usage data:
Information about how you interact with the website, including pages visited, session duration, device type, browser type, and interaction events. This data is collected automatically and is used in aggregated or anonymized form where possible.

Optional information:
You may choose to provide additional information (such as preferences or context about your use case). Providing this information is not required.

‍

‍

2. How We Use Your Information

We use your personal information for the following purposes:

  • To respond to your inquiries and messages
  • To process form submissions (e.g. feedback, waitlists, or requests)
  • To improve website content, tools, and user experience
  • To understand user needs and prioritize future features
  • To send updates or communications, only when you have provided your email for that purpose
  • To comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements

Analytics and infrastructure:
EmTalk may use analytics tools (such as Google Analytics or Firebase) to understand how the website is used, improve performance, and enhance user experience. Data is processed in aggregated or anonymized form where possible.

Advertising:
EmTalk does not display ads and does not use personal data for advertising purposes.

If this changes in the future, we will update this Privacy Policy and, where required, request your consent.

‍

3. Sharing of Personal Information

EmTalk does not sell your personal information.

We may share personal data only with:

  • Service providers that help operate the website (such as hosting, analytics, or form processing providers like Google), under confidentiality obligations
  • Legal authorities, when required by law
  • Business partners, in connection with a merger or acquisition, with appropriate safeguards

All third parties are expected to protect your data.

‍

4. Data Security & Retention

We take your privacy seriously. EmTalk uses reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect your personal data.

While no system can guarantee absolute security, we continuously improve our safeguards.

Personal data is retained:

  • for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes described above
  • or as required by applicable law

You may request deletion of your data at any time.

‍

5. Your Privacy Rights

Depending on your location, you may have the right to:

  • Access your data
  • Correct your information
  • Request data deletion
  • Restrict or object to certain data uses
  • Withdraw consent at any time
  • Lodge a complaint with a data protection authority

To exercise your rights, contact us at:
📩 info@emtalk.org

We will respond within a reasonable timeframe.

‍

6. Children’s Privacy

The EmTalk website is not intended for individuals under the age of 18.

We do not knowingly collect personal data from minors. If we become aware that such data has been provided, we will take steps to delete it.

If you believe a minor has shared personal information with us, please contact us.

‍

7. Cookies & Tracking Technologies

EmTalk may use cookies or similar technologies to:

  • understand usage patterns
  • improve performance
  • ensure basic website functionality

These technologies are not used for advertising purposes.

You can manage or disable cookies through your browser settings.

The website may also include forms or call-to-action elements (such as sign-ups or feedback requests). These are not personalized using personal data unless you explicitly provide it.

‍

8. Changes to This Policy

This Privacy Policy is effective as of the date indicated above.

We may update it from time to time to reflect changes to the website, legal requirements, or improvements in clarity.

Material changes may be communicated through the website or other appropriate channels.

‍9. Contact Us

If you have any questions, feedback, or concerns about this Privacy Policy, you may contact us at:

📩 info@emtalk.org

We aim to respond in a timely and transparent manner.

‍

10. Supplemental Notices

EmTalk is available worldwide.

Your personal data may be processed in Kazakhstan or in other countries where our service providers operate.

By using the website, you acknowledge that your data may be transferred to jurisdictions with different data protection standards. Where required, we apply appropriate safeguards (such as Standard Contractual Clauses).

Depending on your location, you may have additional rights under laws such as:

  • GDPR / UK GDPR
  • CCPA / CPRA
  • PIPEDA

We comply with applicable data protection laws.

We comply with applicable data protection laws in the jurisdictions where DM is offered. If you have questions about international data transfers or your regional rights, please contact us at:

📩 info@emtalk.org

‍

‍

sections.contentHtml:
Spielberger State-Trait Anxiety Inventory

Assess both current situational anxiety and your general tendency to experience anxiety. 12 min 40 questions Start

Motivation Test by Gerchikov

Identify your dominant workplace motivation type: instrumental, professional, patriotic, ownership, or lumpenized. 10 min 28 questions Start

Maslach Burnout Inventory

Assess burnout across emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and personal accomplishment based on how often you experience work-related feelings. 10 min 22 questions Start

Mobbing Test

Assess whether workplace bullying, exclusion, humiliation, or deliberate interference may be affecting you in your current job. 7 min 20 questions Start

Social Phobia Inventory (SPIN)

Assess social anxiety symptoms and how strongly social situations affected you during the past week. 5 min 17 questions Start

WHY TAKE A TEST?

A clearer starting point for understanding yourself

These tests turn vague feelings into something easier to reflect on. They can help you recognize recurring patterns, understand their intensity, and decide whether rest, a conversation, or professional support may be useful.

01

Notice patterns

See how often certain thoughts, emotions.

02

Find the words

Use the result as a prompt for journaling or a more focused conversation.

03

Choose a next step

Receive practical guidance based on your answers and current situation.

Important: self-assessment tests are educational tools, not a medical diagnosis. If symptoms are severe, persistent, or affect daily life, consider speaking with a qualified professional.

sections.contentHtml:
HomeBretDecision MatrixTestsArticlesAbout Us Get Started ↗☰Menu HomeBretDecision MatrixTestsArticlesAbout UsGet Started ↗

Motivation Test by Gerchikov

Identify your dominant workplace motivation type: instrumental, professional, patriotic, ownership, or lumpenized.

0QUESTIONS

10

MINUTES

Answer each question based on your experience at work over the past few months. There are no right or wrong answers.

What do you value most in your job? You can give one or two answers.

I decide what and how to do things myself. It allows me to demonstrate what I know and can do. I feel useful and necessary as an employee. I am paid well for it. I don't particularly value anything, but the job is familiar and comfortable. Multiple choice 2

Which statement suits you best? Give only one answer.

I can provide a decent income for myself and my family. I am the master of my work. I have enough knowledge and experience to handle any difficulties in my job. I always do what is required of me. I am a valuable, indispensable employee for the organization. Single choice

How do you prefer to work? You can give one or two answers.

I prefer to do what is familiar and comfortable. I am ready to do whatever is necessary for the organization. There must always be something new in the job to avoid stagnation. It must be clear what needs to be done and what I will receive for it. I prefer to work with full personal responsibility. Multiple choice 2

What are the main functions of a supervisor, in your opinion? You can give one or two answers.

Ensure team cohesion. Control the progress of the work and make sure everything is done properly. Distribute the work and clearly define who is responsible for what. Assign tasks according to qualifications and ensure material support. Other Multiple choice 2

What does your income represent to you? You can give one or two answers.

It's primarily a reward for my knowledge and qualifications. It's payment for the time and effort spent on the job. Whatever it is, I earned it myself. It's payment for my contribution to the overall success of the organization. I need a guaranteed income, even if it's small, but stable. Multiple choice 2

Salary and bonuses, pensions, scholarships

Very important Not very important Not important at all Single choice

Qualification allowances

Very important Not very important Not important at all Single choice

Allowances for difficult and hazardous working conditions

Very important Not very important Not important at all Single choice

Social benefits and allowances

Very important Not very important Not important at all Single choice

Income from property, shares, investments

Very important Not very important Not important at all Single choice

Any additional earnings

Very important Not very important Not important at all Single choice

Additional earnings only in my specialty

Very important Not very important Not important at all Single choice

Income from personal household or garden

Very important Not very important Not important at all Single choice

Lottery or casino winnings

Very important Not very important Not important at all Single choice

On what principles, in your opinion, should the relationship between the worker and the organization be built? You can give one or two answers.

The worker should treat the organization as their home and share all difficulties and successes. The organization should accordingly value the worker's loyalty and effort. The worker comes to the organization to develop their abilities. The organization should provide this opportunity and benefit from it. The worker spends their energy on the organization, and the organization must guarantee their salary and social benefits. A person works for the organization, but they should do their job on their own; excessive attachment to the team only interferes. The worker sells their labor to the organization, and if they are not given a good price, they have the right to find another buyer. Multiple choice 2

Why do people usually show initiative at work and make various proposals? You can give one or two answers.

They feel special responsibility for their work. They want to win the favor of management. They usually want to improve the organization's work. They want to realize their knowledge and experience, going beyond established work boundaries. They want to earn money, since any useful initiative should be rewarded. Multiple choice 2

Which statement about collective work is closer to your opinion? You can give one or two answers.

You can work in a team, but payment should be based on personal results. I like working in a team — I can always rely on a colleague, and if things go wrong, we'll deal with it together. I prefer to work autonomously, but I can also work in a team of professionals. I need freedom of action, but the team often limits this freedom. Teamwork is very important to me, it is impossible to achieve significant results alone. Multiple choice 2

How do you deal with difficulties at work? You can give one or two answers.

I turn to my manager. I am ready to solve complex issues because my salary depends on it. I am obliged to handle difficulties on my own in the work assigned to me. We solve complex issues as a team. The team is a great force, any difficulties are manageable. I have enough knowledge and experience to handle difficulties. Multiple choice 2

If you were temporarily not working and could choose a new job, what would you choose? You can give one or two answers.

The most interesting, creative one. The most independent and autonomous one. The one with the highest pay. The one with not too heavy work and, although small, a guaranteed income. I would return to my previous workplace because we have a great team. Multiple choice 2

What, in your opinion, determines the promotion of an employee? You can give one or two answers.

Whether the employee is valuable and indispensable to the organization. Their connections and acquaintances. How their level of professionalism grows. How responsibly they approach any task assigned to them. Their ability to behave correctly with management. Multiple choice 2

Which statement about control best suits your opinion? You can give one or two answers.

Control is necessary because some workers may slack off. Control is needed primarily for the benefit of the whole business. Control only hinders work; a good worker knows what and how to do. I recognize only professional control. Without control, it's hard to determine who did how much and what they should get for it. Multiple choice 2

Which statement about work quality best suits your opinion? You can give one or two answers.

The quality of our work is very important because, in the end, it determines the organization's reputation. Don't slack off, but the quality of my work depends on the resources and conditions I have. You need to meet the requirements because mistakes and defects are punished. Quality is especially important when it's paid extra. A professional cannot do a bad job, so quality is important all the time, even if the customer can't appreciate it. Multiple choice 2

What do you think is the main cause of misunderstanding and conflicts between management and employees? You can give one or two answers.

Lack of professionals — among both employees and managers. They care more about personal interests than the company's interests, which harms the overall business. Dissatisfaction with unfair pay, so people don't work as well as they could. Management is more often to blame — they don't provide normal working conditions but still demand results. Management intervenes too much in matters where the employee knows better. Multiple choice 2

If you are a manager, what attracts you the most about this position? You can give one or two answers.

The ability to make independent decisions. High pay. The ability to bring the greatest benefit to the organization. The ability to organize the work of others. The best way to apply my knowledge and skills. Multiple choice 2

If you are not a manager, would you like to become one? You can give one or two answers.

Yes, because it will give me the opportunity to make independent and responsible decisions. Yes, if it is paid accordingly. I don't mind if it's needed for the greater good. Yes, why not? Yes, because I will be able to better apply my knowledge and skills. Multiple choice 2

If the situation at your workplace deteriorates, what changes in your work and position would you agree to in order to keep your job? You can give as many answers as you like.

Learn a new profession. Work part-time or take a lower-paid, less qualified job. Switch to a less convenient work schedule. Work more intensively. I'll just endure it because there's nowhere else to go. Multiple choice
